title: Stamp the handoff with the commit it describes

validator.title: Stamp the handoff with the commit it describes
validator.root_cause: Established by a controlled experiment. In the scale A/B, unstamped (OLD) resumers judged 'does the summary cover this commit?' inconsistently: the same scenario drew different answers across replicates. With the stamp, coverage becomes a mechanical fact (stamped-handoff-scale.md, 'The 11 OLD misses, read by hand').
validator.evidence: All figures match the record. There were 88 agents (11 branches x {STALE, CURRENT} x 2 arms x 2 replicates). Accuracy was OLD 33/44 vs NEW 44/44 (Fisher p = 0.0005), and 10 of the 11 misses were over-reports. Tokens were x0.83 overall (CI 0.68-1.00, p = 0.023) and x0.69 in the CURRENT case (0.57-0.84, p = 0.010). The STALE case was x0.94 (0.71-1.23, p = 0.58), so the pilot's saving did not replicate. The pilot was n = 4 per arm on one branch, -31 % turns, -33 % tokens. One limit is omitted: the record says 'Accuracy is partly definitional for NEW. The stamp defines coverage, so NEW's 44/44 means consistent with the stamp', not better unaided judgment. The STALE variants were also synthetic.
validator.battle_tested: Not yet. The stamp was adopted 2026-09-28 (DEVLOG 1749), the same day as the experiments. Production use so far is one wave (70), e.g. the U2 finisher whose status_delta reported STALE by 1 (DEVLOG 1759). DEVLOG 1759 itself lists the stamped handoff as 'Kept, but first in the validation queue', and production measurement 'continues under PB1698'. The controlled evidence is strong, but sustained production use and a measured production effect are absent.
validator.missing: Production evidence across later waves (70+ under PB1698): resume accuracy and orientation cost for real resumers and successors that used status_delta.py, with no reversal. The strongest candidate for promotion once that data exists.
validator.correction: Add the record's limits: NEW accuracy is partly definitional (consistency with the stamp), the STALE variants were synthetic, the sample is 11 branches from one project and one model, and the task measured orientation only, not downstream work.

validator.battle_tested: Yes. validator.correction: State the scope explicitly. The single allocator must cover EVERY orchestrator, local and cloud (PB1537/PB1546, 2026-09-24), and must read next-free from the tree at allocation time, never from a memory or checkpoint snapshot (PB939/PB950, 2026-09-21).

refuter.reason:

But it was not shown to prevent the failure it targets: collisions kept recurring after adoption on 2026-09-02 (Entry 1430).

kb/Work ids:
- PB315–PB370 were renumbered the same evening (Entry 1437: 'arriving anyway because two lanes allocated in parallel').

- The orchestrator itself allocated PB939 from a memory snapshot; it became PB950 (Entry 1628, 09-21).

Determination ids:

- D18 became D19 (Entry 1544).

- D-DL2 became D-DL3 (Entry 1648, 09-22).

refuter.title: Practices kept in prose are forgotten: one practices file, rendered briefs, a checker
refuter.reason:
The facts check out. Entry 1664 (09-23) records that wave 58 depended on the make_w58 → w52 → w48 scratchpad chain plus GATE-WAIT.txt, and that the briefs lacked pipelining, STOP and the blocking wait. check_practices.py was RED (6) on the old briefs and RED on the hand-rendered spec, then GREEN.

The checker is in steady use: it runs in the CI audits job and was extended for P10, P11, I7, O2 and O8, with each new check shown to fail once. But no production catch is recorded. Every RED in DEVLOG is a self-test at creation or extension, and a gate that has only ever passed since then shows nothing about whether it helped.

Later primary sources also contradict the cure the title implies:
- The ledger refresh has been in the one practices file since the commit that created it (O2 text, ed699e767, 09-23). It was skipped at seven consecutive GAP-moving landings (trains 65–70b, 09-27 to 09-28) and at the battery #87 close. Orchestrator practices are outside what check_practices checks.
- PB1701: P4 was in the file and in every checked brief, yet 3 of 14 finished branches (21 %) ended stale — 'a written rule that fails silently'.
- P1 as written put clerks on Opus until 09-27.

The checker proves a brief contains the words, not that anyone follows them. Missing: a recorded production case where the checker stopped a dispatch that had dropped a practice, or a before/after measure of compliance. The claim should be narrowed to keeping briefs complete, not to keeping practices remembered.

validator.battle_tested: No. The fix is a prose rule that already existed (the DEVLOG ordering note and CLAUDE.md rule 6 say to take the stamp from `date`), and it failed repeatedly.
